questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few deposits are bonds. Some bonds are accounts. All accounts are cards.
Conclusions:
I. All deposits are cards.
II. No bonds is a cards.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: No deposits is a bonds. Some bonds are accounts. All accounts are cards.
Conclusions:
I. All deposits are cards.
II. Some cards are bonds.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some deposits are bonds. All bonds are accounts. No accounts is a cards.
Conclusions:
I. Some deposits are accounts.
II. Some bonds are cards.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few deposits are bonds. All bonds are accounts. No accounts is a cards.
Conclusions:
I. Some deposits are not bonds.
II. No bonds is a cards.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
Statements: V < P = W < X > Q.
Conclusions: I. Q ≤ X   II. X > V.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is definitely true; II is definitely true. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
Statements: Q < W = U = X = P.
Conclusions: I. U ≥ X   II. W < P.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is definitely true; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:

Conclusions: I. T > Q   II. S < X.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:

Conclusions: I. Q < P   II. S ≤ Q.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is definitely true. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
rural savings digital = mi to ka
rural banking growth = pa ze ka
savings banking secure = ze ni to
digital growth secure = ni pa mi
rural savings secure = ni to ka
What is the code for “rural”?
questions.explanation: Answer: ka. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: rural = ka, savings = to, digital = mi, banking = ze, growth = pa, secure = ni.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 79 km east, turns left and walks 76 km, then turns left and walks 22 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 95. Net displacement is 57 km east and 76 km north. By Pythagoras, √(57² + 76²) = 95 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 36 km east, turns left and walks 40 km, then turns left and walks 6 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 50. Net displacement is 30 km east and 40 km north. By Pythagoras, √(30² + 40²) = 50 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 55 km east, turns left and walks 68 km, then turns left and walks 4 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 85. Net displacement is 51 km east and 68 km north. By Pythagoras, √(51² + 68²) = 85 km.

questions.stem: H is the mother of E. B is the son of E. G is the father of E. How is B related to G?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. G is a parent of E, and B is E’s son. Hence B is G’s grandchild.

questions.stem: F is the brother of G. G is the mother of B. H is the father of F and G. How is F related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. F is the brother of B’s mother G. Therefore F is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: D is the only daughter of F. F is the father of D. A is the son of D. C is the sister of F. How is F related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. F is the father of D, and D is A’s mother. Thus F is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 64 candidates, a candidate is 10th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 52. New front rank = 10+3 = 13. Back rank = 64 − 13 + 1 = 52.

questions.stem: In a queue of 43 candidates, a candidate is 20th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 20. New front rank = 20+4 = 24. Back rank = 43 − 24 + 1 = 20.

questions.stem: An item costs ₹1400. It is marked above cost and sold at a 20% discount on marked price, earning 20% profit. Find the marked price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 2100. Selling price = 1400 × 120/100. Marked price = selling price ÷ 0.8 = 2100.

questions.stem: A can finish a job in 32 days and B in 48 days. They work together for 4 days, then B leaves. How many more days does A need? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 25.33. Use 96 work units. Rates: A = 3, B = 2 units/day. Remaining = 96 − 4×5. Divide by A’s rate 3.

questions.stem: A vessel contains 65 litres of milk and water in ratio 3:2. How many litres of pure milk must be added to make the ratio 2:1?
questions.explanation: Answer: 13. Milk = 3V/5, water = 2V/5. Solve (3V/5 + x)/(2V/5) = 2; x = V/5 = 13.

questions.stem: The average of 29 numbers is 64. One number, 76, is replaced and the average rises by 5. What is the new number?

questions.stem: A father is three times as old as his daughter. After 4 years, their combined age will be 104 years. Find the father’s present age.
questions.explanation: Answer: 72. Let daughter’s age be x. Father is 3x. 4x + 8 = 104; x = 24, so father = 72.
